'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#D2B1D9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50%}} | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Mary Peltola]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Nick Begich III]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsAK}}The '''2024 United States House of Representatives election in Alaska''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States House of Representatives]] to represent the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Alaska]] from its {{ushr|AK|AL|D}}. The election coincided with the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 U.S. presidential election]], [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the U.S. House, [[2024 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], and various other [[2024 United States elections|state and local elections]]. Incumbent [[Mary Peltola]], the first [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] to represent Alaska in the House since [[1972 United States House of Representatives election in Alaska|1972]], sought a second full term in office. Peltola had been elected in an [[2022 Alaska's at-large congressional district special election|August 2022 special election]] to succeed deceased [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Don Young]]. She [[2022 United States House of Representatives election in Alaska|won a full term]] the following November. In accordance with [[2020 Alaska Measure 2]], the race was conducted using the state's [[instant-runoff voting|ranked-choice voting]] procedures. Eleven candidates challenged Peltola in the August all-party primary. Republicans [[Nick Begich III]], [[Nancy Dahlstrom]], and Matthew Salisbury initially qualified for spots in the ranked-choice general election, but Dahlstrom and Salisbury withdrew shortly after the primary in a show of party unity.{{cite news |last1=Acuña Buxton |first1=Matt |title=A dozen candidates have dropped out of Alaska’s general election |url=https://thealaskacurrent.com/2024/09/04/a-dozen-candidates-have-dropped-out-of-alaskas-general-election/ |access-date=November 26, 2024 |work=The Alaska Current |date=September 4, 2024}} The final general election ballot thus featured Peltola, Begich, [[Alaskan Independence Party]] nominee John Wayne Howe, and Democrat [[Eric Hafner]]. The Alaska Democratic Party attempted to have Hafner removed from the ballot due to his status as a federal prisoner in [[New York (state)|New York]], but the [[Alaska Supreme Court]] rejected their arguments. Given Alaska's [[political party strength in Alaska|conservative lean]], Peltola was considered a top target for Republicans throughout the cycle.{{cite news |last1=Ruskin |first1=Liz |title=Peltola is a GOP target. She’s stepped up her campaign fundraising. |url=https://alaskapublic.org/2023/08/03/peltola-is-a-gop-target-shes-stepped-up-her-campaign-fundraising/ |access-date=November 26, 2024 |work=Alaska Public Media |date=August 3, 2023}} By late October, multiple outlets regarded Peltola as one of the 10 most vulnerable incumbents running for reelection in the House.{{cite news |last1=Klein |first1=Matthew |title=Hot to Go: The 10 Most Vulnerable House Incumbents of 2024 |url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/analysis/house/house-overview/hot-go-10-most-vulnerable-house-incumbents-2024 |access-date=November 26, 2024 |work=The Cook Political Report with Amy Walter |date=October 30, 2024}}{{cite news |last1=Altimari |first1=Daniela |last2=McIntire |first2=Mary Ellen |title=Tight House races make for crowded Most Vulnerable Incumbent list |url=https://rollcall.com/2024/10/29/tight-house-races-make-for-crowded-most-vulnerable-incumbent-list/ |access-date=November 26, 2024 |work=Roll Call |date=October 29, 2024}} Despite Peltola's loss, she outperformed [[Kamala Harris]] in the concurrent [[2024 United States presidential election in Alaska|2024 presidential election in Alaska]] by about 10 points. Begich was declared the winner on November 20, following the tabulation of ranked-choice votes.{{cite news |last1=Bohrer |first1=Becky |title=Trump-backed Republican Nick Begich beats Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola for Alaska’s only House seat |url=https://apnews.com/article/peltola-begich-alaska-house-e57bf9cf11a2668ffe67e40d840979f2 |access-date=November 26, 2024 |work=Associated Press |date=November 20, 2024}} He was sworn in on January 3, 2025.{{Cite web |date=2025-01-04 |title=Nick Begich III is sworn in as Alaska's representative in the U.S. House |url=https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/washington-d-c/2025-01-03/nick-begich-iii-is-sworn-in-as-alaskas-representative-in-the-u-s-house |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=Alaska Public Media |language=en}} ==Candidates== ===Democratic Party=== ====Advanced to general==== *[[Eric Hafner]], federal prisoner and perennial candidate{{Cite news |work=[[Alaska Beacon]] |access-date=September 5, 2024 |url=https://alaskabeacon.com/2024/09/04/alaska-democrats-sue-to-remove-imprisoned-out-of-state-democrat-from-u-s-house-ballot/ |date=September 4, 2024 |author=Brooks, James |title=Alaska Democrats sue to remove imprisoned out-of-state Democrat from U.S. House ballot}} *[[Mary Peltola]], incumbent U.S. representative{{cite web|last=Fortinsky|first=Sarah|title=Alaska's GOP lieutenant governor joins race against Dem Rep.
